headline: Highest risk is medium: Haystack’s broad egress/MCP plus Rasa’s external channel integrations create plausible prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error paths, but no direct shared workspace is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, and Rasa can ingest messages from Slack, Telegram, Twilio, and similar channels. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if Haystack output is routed into Rasa or vice versa, but the profiles do not document a default shared channel or direct parsing path, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF Haystack output is forwarded into Rasa message handlers without sanitization
IF either agent treats external text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable any automatic handoff from Haystack to Rasa
Add a strict content filter that strips imperative text before forwarding
Require human review for any cross-agent prompt content
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call APIs, while Rasa connects to third-party messaging platforms and handles text/voice. If either agent processes sensitive conversation content in a shared workflow, data can leave the local boundary. The profiles do not show secrets handling or a shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF sensitive user text is routed through Haystack before reaching Rasa
IF either agent forwards full message context to an external API
mitigations: Minimize payloads sent between agents
Redact PII before any API call
Restrict Haystack egress to approved endpoints only
Log and review outbound message samples
requires-engineering: separate sensitive and non-sensitive workflows

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack exposes API-calling surfaces and broad egress, while Rasa does not support multiple instances and is not documented as writing shared state. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same filesystem, git repo, or OAuth scopes, so a direct capability conflict is not evidenced; only a limited coordination risk remains.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same mutable resource
IF an orchestrator gives them overlapping write permissions
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces
Use file or job locks around shared resources
Avoid concurrent writes to the same bot configuration
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG system, so its outputs are likely to be consumed by downstream logic, and Rasa is a customer-support bot that can act on dialogue. If Rasa treats Haystack-generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect responses or actions. The profiles do not prove this default linkage, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Rasa uses Haystack answers as authoritative without verification
IF Haystack-generated content is inserted into customer replies
mitigations: Add a verification step before Rasa responds
Require citations or source links for Haystack answers
Route low-confidence answers to a human agent
Track and reject unsupported claims
requires-engineering: implement confidence-based gating

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack is documented as touching anonymous usage statistics, while Rasa handles text and voice and integrates with external messaging channels. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, and no PHI or EU PII is explicitly shown, so compliance risk is limited to potential policy gaps rather than a confirmed breach.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is introduced into either agent
IF retention or logging policies differ across the connected channels
mitigations: Confirm retention settings for both systems
Disable unnecessary transcript logging
Document data-class handling for each channel
Review vendor DPAs before deployment
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
